answer.rationale: The incumbent has refused to reopen price, so renew/negotiate paths cannot meet the 18% mandate this cycle. The low-cost vendor's quote meets the mandate alone. Memory_c2 supports that a prior switch to this vendor succeeded on cost, onboarding speed, and invoicing accuracy — that is the one legacy claim I want re-verified before committing, because the memory text is thin and a full migration carries delivery risk. Memory_c3 supports that dual-sourcing protects against single-point-of-failure; I flag it as a follow-up next review, but cannot pursue it this cycle. The primary delivery risk is the 14-day window and the lack of buffer at 94% capacity. Mitigation: structure the switch as a phased transition (retain incumbent on a short month-to-month bridge per the pattern in memory_c5) so that if the new vendor's first shipment slips, the line is not exposed. This keeps total cost of ownership on a downward path while capping delivery risk. No other action this cycle achieves the mandated cost target.
